To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ADC(0,500) and f′, but not ADC(0, 800) or D′, allow a differentiation between CA, NET, and CP, and that ADC(0.500) and f' differ between the healthy head, body, tail, and CA.
diffusion-weighted imaging with three b values is able to distinguish between different pancreatic diseases, including pancreatic cancer.

the intravoxel in-coherent motion–based characterization of the diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging signal of pancreatic masses with three b-values improves the diagnostic accuracy in the discrimination of pancreatic adenocarcinaomas from neuroendocrine tumors, chronic pancreatitis and healthy pancreas.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel, highly efficient and accurate algorithm for the analysis of diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance images of the pancreas, which allows to determine the diffusion properties of tissue and its microcirculation.
the use of diffusion weighted imaging (DWI), which is an MRI sequence that can be used for imaging tumors, to distinguish pancreatic adenocarcinaomas from neuroendocrine tumors.
the diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI)-based characterization of pancreatic lesions and the healthy pancreas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ADC(0, 50) and f’ are superior to ADC(0,80) in the differentiation of CAs from other pathologic entities and that ADC(0.50) is the most sensitive parameter for the differentiation of C.A from healthy pancreatic parenchyma.
IVIM model-based DWI with 1.5 T can improve the characterization of pancreatic tumors and the healthy tissue, but the results have to be confirmed by prospective studies.
the 3 b-value IVIM model–based analysis of DWI data significantly improved the characterization of pancreatic tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3 b-value IVIM analysis provides additional diagnostic information for pancreatic diseases.
DWI with 2 b values is sufficient for the characterization of CAs, whereas DWI with 5 or 3 b values should be used for the characterization of NETs and CPs, respectively.
the IVIM model–based characterization with 3 b-value DWI is a promising method for pancreatic tumor diagnosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of ADC(0,80) and D′ is the best way to discriminate pancreatic adenocarcincoma from neuroendocrine tumors, chronic pancreatitis, and the healthy pancreas.

the combination of ADC(0,500) and f′ is a promising tool for the discrimination of pancreatic masses from healthy pancreas and other pancreatic diseases, and that the combination of the ADC(50,800) and f′ provides a promising tool for discrimination of pancreatic masses.
the use of 3 b-values DWI and the IVIM model can be a useful tool for the differential diagnosis of pancreatic lesions.
